I've been working this land in Quzhou for over three decades. The soil here is loam, deep, and I know every corner of my 18.4 mu. My cropping system centers on cotton — that's been my main cash income since the 1990s. The rest I run as wheat-maize double-cropping, which gives me grain security and steady returns when cotton prices dip.

With just two of us in the household and my wife doing some off-farm work, I can't afford to waste time on inefficient practices. I'll use well irrigation carefully — electricity costs have gone up, so I won't irrigate more than necessary, but I won't let the crops suffer either.

**Cotton (8 mu):** I'll plant a hybrid BT variety again — I've used it for years and the pest pressure from bollworm is manageable. I'll rotary till in April, apply base fertilizer, and plant in late April. I'll irrigate four times: pre-plant, bud stage, peak flowering, and boll-filling. Pesticide applications will run about 5 times (aphids and spider mites are my main headaches here). I expect around 280 kg seed cotton per mu in a normal year.

**Winter wheat (10.4 mu):** I'll plough after maize harvest in October to break up the pan layer — I do this every two years and this is the year for it. I'll use an improved semi-dwarf variety like Jimai 22, which performs well in this county. Four irrigations: seeding water, overwintering, jointing, and heading. Nitrogen split between base and jointing topdress. Targeting 480 kg/mu.

**Summer maize (10.4 mu, same land as wheat):** Right after wheat harvest in June I'll direct-seed a hybrid — Xianyu 335 or Zhengdan 958 — no-till to save time and moisture. Only two irrigations needed if summer rains cooperate; I'll add a third at silking if it's dry. Pesticide twice: corn borer treatment and a herbicide pass. Targeting 570 kg/mu.
